description: Danna Arrieta-Ventura reflects on her family’s personal connections to 9/11 and its aftermath. Her mother had immigrated from Peru and was studying in high school in New York in 2001. Because communication between the family in the United States and relatives in Peru was limited, her mother spoke with them only every week or two. When the attacks happened, her great-aunt was in Lima, where people listened to the radio and followed events; she feared for the mother’s safety while unable to contact her. The speaker also recounts a middle-school science teacher’s story about a hijab-wearing friend who worked near the World Trade Center and was surrounded and hidden by coworkers and friends in New York in the weeks afterward. She describes the aftermath as having a broad cultural impact and causing fear in the United States and internationally. The recording is part of the UCF Remembers 9/11 collection and was recorded September 11, 2026.
